History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
27-year-old man presents minutes after an insect sting to the right arm with localized rash and self-reported mild breathing concern; examination suggests a localized allergic reaction without systemic involvement.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Mild difficulty breathing (subjective) and possible lip swelling after a bee/wasp sting.  
• Onset: Sting occurred “a few minutes ago” prior to video consultation.  
• Course/progression: Patient notes anxiety about potential worsening but currently feels breathing is “not particularly acute.” Rash limited to sting site; no progressive swelling observed.  
• Location of sting: Right arm with puncture mark, slight redness/blotchiness, no appreciable swelling on video.  
• Associated symptoms: “Tongue feels a bit weird,” slight lip soreness on right side. No stridor, wheeze, chest tightness, or generalized urticaria reported.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None taken yet; no antihistamine use prior to call.  
• Review of systems (pertinent):  
  – Respiratory: Subjective mild dyspnea; normal speech; no audible wheeze/stridor observed by clinician.  
  – ENT: No visible lip/tongue swelling on exam.  
  – Skin: Localized erythematous rash at puncture site; no generalized rash.  
  – Cardiovascular/GI/Neurologic: Not specifically queried; no related complaints.

Past Medical History:
• Eczema (history).  
• Anxiety/panic episodes (never medicated).  

Medications:
• None currently; no antihistamines taken yet.

Allergies:
• Penicillin (reaction details not specified).

Social History:
• Employment: Computer scientist.  
• Living situation: Lives alone.  
• Pets: Owns a cat.  
• Smoking/alcohol/substance use: Not discussed.

Family History:
• No relevant familial illnesses or acute allergic reactions reported.

Physical Examination: (video)
• General: Alert, speaking full sentences, no distress.  
• Airway/Breathing: Normal work of breathing; no visible lip or tongue swelling; normal phonation; no stridor heard.  
• Skin: Right arm puncture mark with mild surrounding erythema; no obvious swelling.  
• Vitals: Not provided.

Investigations:
• None performed; assessment based on video inspection.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (no current systemic/anaphylactic features)  
  • Educated patient on signs of anaphylaxis: lip/tongue swelling, stridor, progressive dyspnea.  
  • Advised over-the-counter oral antihistamine: chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet, up to six times daily OR once-daily non-sedating antihistamine (dose/route/frequency per product instructions).  
  • If rash spreads, becomes hot, or infection suspected → seek medical review for possible antibiotics.  
  • If any airway compromise or rapid progression → call emergency services / attend A&E immediately.  
  • Provided online information link regarding anaphylaxis.

Issue 2 – Anxiety related to acute event  
  • Reassured regarding low likelihood of systemic reaction given stable status several minutes post-sting.  
  • Encouraged low threshold to re-contact service for reassurance if symptoms or anxiety worsen.

General plan items  
  • No current need for EpiPen or formal allergy testing; consider if future systemic reactions occur.  
  • Follow-up: Patient to self-monitor; return if symptoms progress or recurrent events develop.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: vitals, complete medication list beyond antihistamines, comprehensive systems review, immunization status.  
• No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational fillers removed.
